newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-CRA expects Bougainville offer soon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-CRA expects Bougainville offer soon.

text.p: CRA Ltd said on Monday it expected it would shortly receive a formal approach from the Papua New Guinea government to buy its stake in Bougainville Copper Ltd.

In a statement to the Australian Stock Exchange, CRA repeated that it was aware of a statement by PNG Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan stating that his government was approaching CRA with a view to purchasing its full interest in the company but had received no proposal from the government.
Bougainville Copper operated the giant Panguna mine on the island for 17 years until a secessionist rebellion led to its closure in 1989.
"On the basis of the prime minister's statement, CRA expects to receive a formal approach from the PNG government shortly," the company said.
"CRA is obliged to consider any such approach on behalf of shareholders on its merits."
The miner also repeated that it has held no discussions with the PNG government about the purchase of its interest in the mine, and said no meetings have been held or arranged.
Chan said in a statement on Sunday that the proposal was part of an initiative to find "a satisfactory and lasting solution to the Bougainville crisis".
Papua New Guinea has been fighting seccessionist rebels on the island province for the past nine years.
Chan said media attention to military training, including the hiring of mercenaries, by PNG defence forces had forced the government to announce its plans prematurely.
CRA has estimated it would cost more than 450 million kina (US$328 million) to restart the mine.
CRA, the Australian part of Anglo-Australia dual listed mining giant RTZ-CRA, owns 53.6 percent of Bougainville Copper.
